# SF Safety Map

> A free, open-source map of San Francisco crime and safety. Search any SF address
> and see real SFPD incident reports nearby — filterable by crime type and time
> window, updated nightly. No ads, no tracking, no accounts.

Live site: https://zihuitommywang.github.io/sf-safety-map/
Source code: https://github.com/ZihuiTommyWang/sf-safety-map

## Key facts

- Data source: San Francisco Police Department incident reports, via DataSF's
  public dataset "Police Department Incident Reports: 2018 to Present"
  (https://data.sf.gov/d/wg3w-h783). Refreshed nightly.
- Coverage: the most recent 3 years (~150,000+ incidents); the map defaults to
  showing the most recent year.
- Only place-based safety incidents are shown. Administrative records (warrants,
  lost property, traffic stops), fraud, shoplifting, and other non-place-based
  reports are filtered out. Incidents are grouped into 13 categories such as
  Assault, Robbery, Theft, Car Break-In & Damage, Burglary, Drugs, and Street
  Disorder.
- Every dot on the map is one real incident report — nothing is smoothed or
  interpolated. Searching an address shows the incident count within 300 m
  compared to a typical SF location, plus the most recent reports.
- Address search covers every official San Francisco address (from the city's
  Enterprise Addressing System) plus places via OpenStreetMap.

## Caveats

- Reported incidents are not a perfect measure of risk: report density also
  reflects police presence, foot traffic, and reporting habits.
- SFPD anonymizes incident locations to the block or intersection level.

## Data files

- Incidents (columnar JSON): https://zihuitommywang.github.io/sf-safety-map/data/incidents.json
- Metadata and category definitions: https://zihuitommywang.github.io/sf-safety-map/data/meta.json
